title: Change of condensed coefficients
statement:
Let $a\colon\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ be a morphism of commutative condensed rings
([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). For a scheme $X$, the *coefficient change* on $X$ is

$$
a_X:=p_X^*a\colon\Lambda_X\longrightarrow\Lambda'_X ,
$$

the image of $a$ under the inverse image $p_X^*$ from the point
([sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]), a morphism between the coefficient ring objects
$\Lambda_X=p_X^*\Lambda$, $\Lambda'_X=p_X^*\Lambda'$ of $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$
([sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]). It is a morphism of ring objects, and it is
functorial in $a$: $(\mathrm{id}_\Lambda)_X=\mathrm{id}_{\Lambda_X}$ and
$(b\circ a)_X=b_X\circ a_X$. The coefficient change induces the derived extension of scalars
([sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars])

$$
T^X:=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-=L(\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X})\colon
D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\longrightarrow D(\Mod_{\Lambda'_X}),
$$

between the derived categories ([sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]) of the module categories of
[sk-def-sfb-module-objects]; it is left adjoint to the levelwise restriction of scalars
$D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$.

For a morphism of schemes $f\colon X\to Y$ let $f^*$, $f_*$ be the pullback and pushforward of
abelian sheaves ([def-sfb-finite-upper-star], [def-sfb-finite-lower-star]), and let
$\alpha_f\colon f^*\Lambda_Y\to\Lambda_X$, $\eta_f\colon\Lambda_Y\to f_*\Lambda_X$ and
$\alpha'_f$, $\eta'_f$ be the coefficient morphisms of [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms] for
$\Lambda$ and for $\Lambda'$. The coefficient changes are compatible with them: the two squares

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
f^*\Lambda_Y & \xrightarrow{\ f^*a_Y\ } & f^*\Lambda'_Y\\
{\scriptstyle\alpha_f}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle\alpha'_f}\\
\Lambda_X & \xrightarrow{\ \ a_X\ \ } & \Lambda'_X
\end{array}
\qquad\qquad
\begin{array}{ccc}
\Lambda_Y & \xrightarrow{\ \ a_Y\ \ } & \Lambda'_Y\\
{\scriptstyle\eta_f}\downarrow & & \downarrow{\scriptstyle\eta'_f}\\
f_*\Lambda_X & \xrightarrow{\ f_*a_X\ } & f_*\Lambda'_X
\end{array}
$$

commute, i.e. $\alpha'_f\circ f^*a_Y=a_X\circ\alpha_f$ and $f_*a_X\circ\eta_f=\eta'_f\circ a_Y$.

proof.text: The coefficient change $a_X$ is the morphism of ring objects of [def-sfb-coefficient-map]. Apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-map-id] and [lem-sfb-coefficient-map-comp] to the underlying condensed abelian-group morphisms: their explicit notation is $c_X:=p_X^*c$, and for ring morphisms it agrees with the coefficient change just constructed. In particular the current composition lemma reads $(b\circ a)_X=p_X^*(b\circ a)=p_X^*b\circ p_X^*a=b_X\circ a_X$, with source $\Lambda_X$ and target $\Lambda^{\prime\prime}_X$ (the pullback of $\Lambda^{\prime\prime}$). The identity and composite ring maps have these same underlying arrows, so equality of those arrows gives $(\mathrm{id}_\Lambda)_X=\mathrm{id}_{\Lambda_X}$ and $(b\circ a)_X=b_X\circ a_X$ also as ring-object morphisms. The pulled-back coefficient rings are commutative ring objects by [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], so this construction applies to the given commutative condensed rings.

source.place: first sentence through functoriality of the coefficient change

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with the sheafified tensor product of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. The site is taken on the small skeleton of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed] with coefficient category $\Ab$ gives that $\mathcal C$ is Grothendieck abelian and closed symmetric monoidal, with additive tensor product. To obtain functorial flat resolutions, apply [lem-pc-sites-modules-functorial-flat-cover] to the constant integer sheaf $\underline{\mathbf Z}$. An abelian sheaf has the unique integer action by repeated addition, every additive map preserves it, and a bilinear map is automatically balanced for this action. Thus $\underline{\mathbf Z}$-module sheaves and their tensor products identify with abelian sheaves and the stated tensor product; the flat-cover functor and its natural epic augmentation therefore give a functorial flat cover on $\mathcal C$. Explicitly, put $K_0(M)=M$, $F_n(M)=T(K_n(M))$ and $K_{n+1}(M)=\ker(\pi_{K_n(M)}:F_n(M)\to K_n(M))$ for $n\geq0$. Composing $F_{n+1}(M)\twoheadrightarrow K_{n+1}(M)$ with $K_{n+1}(M)\hookrightarrow F_n(M)$ gives an exact augmented resolution $\cdots\to F_1(M)\to F_0(M)\to M\to0$ by flat objects. Naturality of $\pi$ induces maps on each kernel, so this resolution is functorial in $M$. This verifies the functorial-flat-resolution hypothesis on $\mathcal C$. The commutative ring objects and ring-object morphism $a_X$ supplied by step 1 now satisfy every hypothesis of [sk-def-sfb-derived-extension-of-scalars]. It gives $T^X=\Lambda'_X\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-=L(\operatorname{Ext}_{a_X})$ and the adjunction $T^X\dashv D(\operatorname{Res}_{a_X})$.

source.place: sentence identifying $T^X$ with derived extension of scalars and its adjunction

proof.text: The given morphism $a$ of commutative condensed rings is in particular a morphism of condensed rings, so [lem-sfb-coefficient-pullback-square] applies and gives $\alpha'_f\circ f^*a_Y=a_X\circ\alpha_f$ on underlying abelian sheaves, with source $f^*\Lambda_Y$ and target $\Lambda'_X$. For the second square apply [lem-sfb-coefficient-pushforward-square] to the underlying condensed abelian-group morphism of $a$. Its statement explicitly identifies, for ring morphisms, its $a_T$, $\alpha_f$ and $\eta_f$ with the underlying abelian-sheaf constructions used here. Consequently its equality is precisely $f_*a_X\circ\eta_f=\eta'_f\circ a_Y$, with source $\Lambda_Y$ and target $f_*\Lambda'_X$. These are exactly the two displayed squares, which the item states for abelian-sheaf pullback and pushforward.
